evals.name: csv-dedupe-reliability
evals.prompt: I have two csv exports of customer contacts - contacts_hubspot.csv has columns email,first_name,last_name,phone and contacts_legacy.csv has columns Email Address,Name,Phone Number. I need a python script that merges them into one clean contacts_merged.csv and removes duplicates. Watch out: emails might differ in case between systems, and some phone numbers have dashes or spaces. My ops team will run this monthly without me so it can't silently drop people. There are no sample files - write the script and make sure it actually works before you hand it over.
evals.expected_output: Working merge script, verified by execution on generated fixture data, assumptions surfaced, success criteria defined, SESSION.md created (with skill)

evals.name: postgres-recommendation
evals.prompt: We're a 15-person startup, cost sensitive, no dedicated ops person. Should we self-host Postgres on a VPS or pay for a managed service like RDS/Supabase/Neon? We store about 50GB now, growing maybe 2x a year, and downtime over an hour would hurt but not kill us. Write me a one-page recommendation (save as postgres_recommendation.md) I can send to my cofounder.
evals.expected_output: One-page recommendation with quantified costs, tradeoffs, steelmanned alternative, flip conditions, labeled confidence

evals.name: trivial-no-ceremony
evals.prompt: quick one - in utils.py rename the function calc_totals to calculate_totals and update its call sites. don't change anything else.
evals.expected_output: Rename done correctly with NO SESSION.md, no ceremony - tests the triage gate

evals.name: code-review-planted-defects
evals.prompt: Review this change before I merge it (before.py -> after.py, diff in change.diff). It adds order item details, pagination, and a payment webhook to our little Flask shop API. Tell me what gates the merge and what can wait.
evals.expected_output: Finds SQL injection, N+1, pagination off-by-one, swallowed webhook exception; zero fabricated blockers; severity + file:line evidence; states not-covered; SESSION.md

evals.name: multi-agent-orchestration-design
evals.prompt: I'm building a multi-agent OS: a planner agent decomposes user requests and dispatches work to specialist agents (coder, reviewer, researcher) that share a workspace filesystem. Design the coordination and state architecture: how work is handed off, how we prevent loops and duplicated work, and how the system recovers when an agent dies mid-task. Write it as a decision-record style doc (orchestration_design.md) I can put in front of a technical cofounder.
evals.expected_output: Explicit topology decision with steelmanned alternative; concrete loop-prevention mechanism; dead-agent recovery (detection + idempotent retry); end-to-end failure walkthrough; flip conditions; SESSION.md

evals.name: product-value-teardown
evals.prompt: Existing product: a Chrome extension that summarizes YouTube videos with AI. 80k installs, 4.2 stars, $4.99/mo with a free tier (3 summaries/day). Recent reviews: praise for lecture/tutorial summaries, complaints that videos over ~1 hour fail, repeated requests to support podcasts (Spotify) and to export summaries to Notion. Churn is highest in month 1. Figure out where the value actually is and give me a prioritized plan (teardown.md) to take this to the next level.
evals.expected_output: Claims labeled observed/inferred/guessed; binding constraint named before solutions; impact x effort x confidence prioritization; metric + kill criterion per bet; non-goals; SESSION.md

evals.name: session-resume-handoff
evals.prompt: PHASE A: Build 'minisite', a tiny stdlib-only Python static site generator: (1) config.py parses site.conf key=value lines (title, author); (2) md.py renders a markdown subset (#/## headers, **bold**, [text](url)); (3) template.py wraps rendered HTML in a page shell using config values; (4) build.py CLI: python3 build.py <srcdir> <outdir> converts content/*.md to <outdir>/*.html. Implement ONLY components 1 and 2, then STOP - you will be interrupted and a DIFFERENT session (that cannot talk to you) will finish the project. PHASE B (fresh agent, same dir): Resume the work and make the whole project work end-to-end per the same spec.
evals.expected_output: Phase B does not rewrite A's modules; follows A's conventions; end-to-end run works; B identified prior state before working; no duplicate implementations

evals.name: real-pr-review-production-repo
evals.prompt: Review a merged PR (provided as pr.diff, ~1000 added lines) that adds consent-ledger, memory-consolidation/confidence-scoring, and user-transparency modules to a privacy-sensitive product, before the modules are wired into production HTTP routes. The PR was written by an AI build agent and merged with green checks. Tell me what the merge gate missed, what must be fixed before production wiring, and what can wait.
evals.expected_output: Grounded review with zero fabricated findings, severity + file/line evidence, consent semantics scrutinized, verification by execution of extractable pure logic, explicit not-reviewed scope, SESSION.md maintained
